children: Insurtech firm Turtlemint Fintech Solutions is expected to clock EBITDA breakeven this fiscal as its operating leverage is at an inflection point.

“A fast-growing policy pool, compounding of renewal book and growth algorithm shifting from recruitment to activation and productivity, the operating leverage is at an inflection point. We expect adjusted EBITDA breakeven in FY27 and margin expansion to around 11 per cent by FY29,” Motilal Oswal Financial Services said in its report on Turtlemint.

The insurtech firm has built a scaled and technology-enabled insurance distribution franchise in the country with over 5.50 lakh certified point of sale persons (PoSPs) providing insurers with a cost-effective means to expand distribution across India’s underserved regions.

“It held around 30 per cent of the market share of PoSPs registered through brokers and around 16 per cent of total PoSPs in FY25. The platform covers an end-to-end distributor journey on a single app. Addition of mutual funds and credit products further makes the platform a one-stop shop for all financial needs of customers,” Motilal Oswal said, adding a fast-growing policy pool and compounding of renewal book should likely lead to renewal revenue contribution rising to over 25 per cent by FY29.
“Supported by higher profitability for renewals, service EBITDA margin should expand to around 22 per cent by FY29 from around 13 per cent in FY26,” it added.

Turtlemint Fintech, in its annual report for FY26, said PoSPs’ contribution to premiums is expected to grow at 24-32 per cent CAGR during FY25-FY30, significantly outpacing the industry’s growth rate of 10-12 per cent. With over 80 per cent of Digital Partners based in B30+ markets and the large certified PoSP network in the country, the company’s tech-enabled PoSP model is well positioned.

“Against this backdrop, we see three clear priorities for the years ahead. First, to continue growing and deepening our digital partner network, particularly in B30+ markets. Second, to advance our technology capabilities — especially in AI — to give our partners an ever-stronger edge. And third, to expand our product catalog thoughtfully: insurance first and always, but also complementary financial products such as mutual funds, loans, credit and deposits, which deepen our relationship with customers and partners alike,” Dhirendra Mahyavanshi, Chairperson, Managing Director and CEO, and Anand Prabhudesai, Executive Director and COO, said in the annual report.

title: Turtlemint expected to clock EBITDA breakeven this fiscal
